Subject: RE: Brightline redlines — proposed MSA/Order Form language (first pass)

Sean / Ellen — first pass below. I’ve tried to balance Brightline’s ask for clear ownership/control with Redwood’s need to continue improving our platform. Comments inline in parentheses; I’ll also attach a tracked-changes doc for legal review.

1) Output ownership (Order Form / Definitions):
"Customer Output" means content, artifacts, or data generated solely as a result of the Customer’s use of the Service in response to Customer-provided prompts or inputs, excluding (a) system-level templates, prompts, or sample outputs provided by Redwood, and (b) outputs derived from model updates that incorporate aggregated, de-identified insights from the wider customer population.

Redwood will not claim ownership of Customer Output. Customer is granted a perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide, non-exclusive right to use, reproduce, and display Customer Output. (We keep a carveout for model-level improvements.)

2) Training and feedback license (MSA — Data Use; optional Order Form election):
- By default, Redwood will not use Customer Content (including Customer Output) to train or improve Redwood models.
- Customer may opt in to a "Feedback Program" by executing an opt-in provision in the Order Form that grants Redwood a limited, perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide, non-exclusive license to use feedback (as defined) to improve Redwood’s models, subject to: (i) data de-identification and aggregation; (ii) no resale or transfer to third parties for model training; and (iii) the right for Customer to revoke participation on 30 days' written notice (revocation will not affect models already trained using previously contributed feedback).

3) Narrow commercial protections (to address Brightline procurement concerns):
- Redwood will provide a contract exhibit documenting the data protection and de-identification controls applied if Customer opts into the Feedback Program.
- For customers requiring stricter segregation, Redwood can offer a Dedicated or Private deployment option (Order Form checkbox) where no cross-customer model training will occur.

Open items for negotiation: whether opt-in is sufficient for Brightline or they require a permanent opt-out/opt-in switch; language around "perpetual" for the feedback license (Brightline prefers tighter temporal limits).

I’ll prepare a tracked-change Word for Ellen’s GC. Aditya — please comment on the technical feasibility of the de-identification and revocation clause below.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Brightline redlines — technical note on training & de-id feasibility

Laura / Sean / Ellen — quick technical notes to support the proposed legal language:

- De-identification: We can run a structured pipeline to strip PII and apply deterministic hashing for identifiers, then aggregate examples to remove low-frequency signals. That will materially reduce the risk of re-identification for model training. We should avoid promising perfect anonymization.

- Revocation: Practically, we can stop future ingestion of new customer feedback once revocation is effective. However, we cannot retroactively remove traces from models already trained on prior feedback (statistical unlearning is an active area but not yet production-ready for large LLM models at scale). Language should reflect that revocation applies prospectively.

- Dedicated/Private deployments: If Brightline chooses a Dedicated pool or Private deployment, we can guarantee no cross-customer training; that is operationally enforceable and should be enumerated as a contractual option (Order Form checkbox).

Suggested clarifying sentence for Laura’s draft: "Customer understands and agrees that revocation of participation in the Feedback Program will prevent use of Customer Data for future model training but will not require Redwood to untrain models or remove statistical contributions from prior training runs."

Happy to provide a short technical addendum for the contract exhibit if that would help their GC.

—Aditya
Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
